comments.body:
There is (or used to be) a very very easy (and cheeky) way to do both clan quests at the same time with almost no effort what-so-ever.

Get a friend, doesn't matter what level they are, the higher the better to be honest, and make a group.

Let your friend do all the killing. [b]DO NOT ATTACK ANY MOB YOURSELF[/b]. You will get rep gain with one clan, but you wont lose any with the other.

This means you can be friendly with both at the same time.

Yeah, you don't get any XP for the killing, nor is it a great deal of fun being your friend's shadow for the ~40 minutes (less now since you start as neutral instead of unfriendly) it took to get friendly, but it is easier, and kinda neat to be friendly with both.

The last time I tried this was pre 2.0.1 and since there was a lot of changes to the rep system in that patch, I have no idea if it works now, and I do believe there are changes in 2.1 which might also affect it, but I'm guessing.

Think the admins were hinting at what they'd like us to do when they titled the Magram quest "Brutal Politics" and the Gelkis quest "Strange Alliance". I.E. brutalize the Magram and ally with the Gelkis? 

I know we don't have to swing it this way, but I'm going that way just to get it over with. 

And I also found Warug at 74,68. North of the main village, in the hills by a bonfire. Can't miss it. ;)

I've done these quest in both directions with a couple characters, and it doesn't really seem to matter either way which one you go with. The relationship you build with one clan just makes a difference as to how easy it'll be to deal with the other one. But as a grinding quest, this one is definitely more fun than killing 200 tigers in STV.

comments.body: The next quest is Assault on the Kolkar, not listed here.

For those wondering whether it is possible in Classic; you cannot be a ghost form and avoid the negative reputation while a party members kills the centaurs (I believe this was possible in original vanilla).

EDIT: You can still do it on classic era.

BORING....I had to kill 200+ centaurs of the other clan to get my rep up high enough to finish this quest.  I started at 2200 rep, and had to raise it to 3000. The thing is, I was only getting 5 rep from each kill, and some would only give me 1!  Only start this quest chain if you are a true grinder.

As a level 36, it appears I am getting +20 rep for the opposing faction, while taking -100 rep for the faction I am killing. You start out at 2000/neutral faction, and you need to get to 3000 to be 'friendly'. So that is a gain of 1000 rep. Consider that you get +20 rep per kill, it will take you 1000/20 or 50 kills in order to gain the proper reputation. This will damage your rep by 50*100=5000 on the other faction. It also appears that you remain neutral until the 2000 drops to zero, which will happen after 20 kills. After that you become 'unfriendly', but you are not kos still at this point. It appears to take another -3000 rep points for that to happen.

So it takes 20 kills to be unfriendly, 50 kills to be hated, and 50 kills to be friendly to the opposing side.

The Magrams are in the southeast. They appear to be slightly lower level.. at least the ones I have seen are 32-33ish so far. The Gelkis are in the southwest, and take a lot longer to get to. The Gelkis are also near a path to the next zone.

I chose to attack the Magrams because they are closer to Nigels Point, they can easily be avoided, they appear to be easier to kill, and they don't guard a path to another zone. There are also a lot of high level 30s near the Gelkis, so it might pay off to have a safe place to run to when fighting down there.

They also drop Centaur ears so you can do Centaur Bounty at the same time.
